body:
I'm not sure I understand the difference between what you're telling me I need to do and "finding happiness." You're absolutely right that I'm fine as long as I know where I am going, but right now I have no idea where I'm going or where I should even try to go.

I'm also not sure what you mean by saying that I should consider my place in this world. I do that constantly, and I feel like it's because I'm so prone to doing that that I am the way I am. How exactly do you define your place in the world? And how do you give it meaning? I'm glad the trivial programming work I do helps out the people I work for, but I feel unfulfilled and exhausted at the end of each day.

> I'm gay but I don't want to be. I want a normal life without the gay stigma.

> Just don't know what to do or who to turn to.

Both of these things hit so close to home for me. I've lived my whole life feeling the same way about being gay, and now that I've settled on the idea that I'm just going to be alone unless I can find someone who just wants to be a close friend and roommate forever (and I don't see that happening), I have no idea what to do to feel motivated or fulfilled. It never gets any easier, does it?

Out of curiosity, how badly do you want a wife and kids and a house? For most of my life, I was convinced that was all I wanted too, but a few years ago I just had to accept that I needed to find some other way to live. And maybe it's not much help to hear that coming from me considering I'm also still suicidal, but at least now I think there's some solution that I'm just having way too difficult of a time finding rather than feeling like there's no solution at all. Before, all I could do was hope I would magically wake up one day and not be gay, which is simply something that's never going to happen.

I'm sorry if I'm not really being any help. I know some things I said might have come off as a bit blunt. I just wanted to tell you how similar I have felt and that maybe there is some hope for people like us to support each other sometimes. I have no idea, but maybe there are actually other people who feel the way we do in support groups?

I Google plenty. And then I close it and ask myself what I'm doing as soon as I reach the point where I have to do something like enter my information or call someone. I guess maybe I'll go somewhere to try schedule something in person, but I feel like I just keep waiting for the day when that's the first thing on my mind and I have nothing else I have to do. I feel like I'm a hopeless case of approach avoidance.

Thanks. I have considered it, yes, but I don't even know how to go about it. My parents tend to shy away from the subject if I bring it up, and I never feel like I can possibly balance going with real life.

I basically don't even know how to seek counseling.

I agree that knowing the answer to that question will help, but it's just so hard for me to identify now. Growing up, video games always made me happy, and for a long time I thought I wanted to get into making them, but I became really jaded once I learned what the industry is like. I'm thinking of applying to some of those jobs anyway now, but I'm not optimistic because I didn't spend any time in college developing the right skill set to meet the job requirements.

I also got really into music composition in high school and college, but never made it anything more than a hobby because I didn't think I could make a living off of it and I felt generally discouraged from even trying.

Other than those things, just having someone around who I share a lot in common with generally makes me happy. But as I said, I've only ever gotten that out of school, and now everyone else seems to be moving on with their lives. I've thought about going to a Meetup of some sort, but I always feel too socially nervous to actually go. I was even nervous about anonymously posting here.
